youtube.title: CRAIG STOBO
youtube.summary: Talking with Paul Brennan, former Financial Markets Authority chair Craig Stobo examines how RNZ’s reported $11.8 million deficit came to be more than 25 times its forecast, raising questions about financial oversight, governance and executive accountability. He discusses the unauthorised overdraft, proposed redundancies, falling cash reserves and the need to reassess the broadcaster’s size, funding and public-service charter. Craig also questions whether RNZ’s role remains justified in today’s diverse media landscape. For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: HELEN JOYCE
youtube.summary: Helen Joyce, Director of Advocacy at Sex Matters, warns that the UK’s proposed conversion practices bill is so broadly drafted that it could criminalise ordinary parenting, religious expression and legitimate therapeutic conversations. She argues that the legislation risks driving therapists away from working with gender-questioning young people, while exposing families to investigations and separation. For further information v isit Sex Matters or find Helen on Substack and X

youtube.title: GARDENING WITH WALLY
youtube.summary: Gardening guru Wally Richards argues that modern farming methods have stripped much of the nutrition from our food, while increasing reliance on artificial fertilisers and chemical sprays. He advocates returning to natural soil-building methods, sharing practical advice on blood and bone, rock minerals, compost tea and homemade plant feeds. For further information: For everything you need to Say No To Gene Tech Wally’s Gardening and Health Products Wally’s Books Garden News NZ To join Wally’s Weekly Garden Newsletter, email Wally at wallyjr@gardenews.co.nz

youtube.title: MAREE’S MUSINGS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke challenges political scientist Lara Greaves’ distinction between legitimate vote splitting and strategic voting, arguing that voters are entitled to use both votes as they see fit under MMP. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: MARGARET CHAMBERS
youtube.summary: Margaret Chambers of Australia’s Institute of Public Affairs warns that the proposed Digital Duty of Care legislation could give the eSafety Commissioner sweeping powers to collect sensitive personal information, profile internet users and share data with overseas enforcement agencies. She argues that vague definitions of harm and broad risk-assessment obligations threaten free expression, privacy and innovation and warns New Zealand not to follow in Australia’s footsteps. For further information: Read the IPA article | How the Digital Duty of Care violates the right to privacy and find the IPA on X, Instagram and Substack Read Margaret’s author page at Spectator Australia or find her on Substack , X and Instagram

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: Rachel Stewart examines the harmful effects of mainstream pornography on young women and men, arguing that it distorts sexual expectations, normalises aggression towards women, damages body image and undermines real-world relationships. She also explores evolutionary biologist Brett Weinstein’s argument that easy access to pornography reduces young men’s motivation to develop the competence and confidence needed to attract a partner. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X
